1.why: All nine screens use a single clean card layout with no moving images, animations, or pop-ups; the only extra element is a static Logs panel.

2.why: Page headings are large and bold, primary actions are solid blue buttons, and the safety notice appears in a highlighted green box on every page.

3.why: Each screen presents one task with one prominent field and button, but the user must also look to the separate Logs panel to retrieve the required codes.

4.why: The flow spans roughly nine steps with a recovery token, two six-digit codes, and password rules (14–128 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and symbol), so many steps and rules must be remembered.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, password-manager integration, or autofill option is visible on any of the nine screens.

6.why: Some fields arrive pre-filled (recovery token, codes) which aids recognition, but no saved-contact, remembered-device, or similar recognition features are shown.

7.why: All text is short and plain, e.g. 'Enter your account email address or international phone number' and the three simple privacy bullet points.

8.why: No user-facing error messages appear in any screenshot; only Logs-panel lines such as 'A password alone is not sufficient. Enter the sign-in MFA code' describe a problem and fix.

9.why: Step 1 provides a concrete example ('name@example.org or +15551234567'), and later steps hint how to proceed, e.g. 'the test code is in the Logs panel' and the password format rule.

10.why: The choices actually offered (email vs. phone, reset link vs. manual token entry, accept checkbox) are clearly labeled, but no face-login option exists.

11.why: Each page offers only one primary button plus at most one secondary link, so the user never faces many simultaneous choices.

12.why: Outcomes are explicitly confirmed at step 2 ('the same confirmation is shown for every request') and step 9 ('Privacy statement accepted'), but intermediate successes such as token verification and password saving are only implied by advancing to the next page.

13.why: Every step carries a short instruction or tip, e.g. 'Tokens are short-lived and can only be used once' and 'For this academic simulation, the test code is in the Logs panel', plus a repeated anti-phishing tip.

14.why: No error states, 'try again', or 'resend code' affordances are shown anywhere, and tokens are described as short-lived and single-use, so easy retry is not demonstrated.

15.why: All nine screens share the identical header, card layout, heading and button styles, and the same repeated safety notice, making the design highly consistent.
